provenance.source_observation: Rebuilt on the reopened branch. Crown apex, image-right bow of the facial centre between brow and cheek, chin exit, spine down the visible back, curved hip handoff and near-vertical far image-left support leg to its boot landing.
Short open crown arc over the top of the cranium only.
Narrow far-side temporal-to-jaw arc, stopping short of the chin so the envelope stays open.
Wider near-side temporal-to-cheek arc; the unequal pair encodes the head turn toward image-right.
Back-three-quarter shoulder rhythm; the near image-right shoulder sits lower and further out.
Hip rhythm tilting down toward the braced image-right leg.

Corrected on the reopened branch. Re-measured against the subject's visible braced-thigh skin band: the chain leaves the hip almost straight down, stays near canvas x=261-265 through the upper thigh, and only then swings image-right through knee and ankle into the wider, lower landing.
Single major axis of the slung rifle, suppressor tip to buttstock at the image-left hip.
The near image-right boot lands lower in frame than the far image-left boot.

provenance.reason: Carried concern: the shoulder axis sat about 13 canvas pixels above the observed far shoulder joint and read as a collar line.
provenance.source_observation: Re-measured shoulder joints from the subject: far image-left joint near canvas (186,163), near image-right joint near canvas (272,172), giving a shallow drop toward the near shoulder.
Pelvis axis between the observed hip joints, tilting down toward the braced leg, counter to the shoulder tilt.
Near image-right arm chain: shoulder joint down the loose sleeve centre to the elbow at the widest jacket point, then a short turn into the wrist and the hand at the hip pocket.
Far image-left arm chain, occluded by the slung rifle; direction read from the visible jacket-left contour and the sleeve end at the jacket hem.

Support-leg chain from the hip joint through a nearly straight knee to the ankle, near-vertical because it carries the weight. It is authored on the same path the verified P1 gesture already states, so it reinforces rather than doubles it.
Braced-leg chain authored on the corrected P1 counterbalance path so the two coincide instead of forming a rail: near-straight upper thigh, then divergence image-right through knee and ankle.
Attached-object extent axis restated from the verified P1 prop axis: suppressor tip to buttstock end.
Prop breadth axis at the scope/receiver, perpendicular to the extent axis, where the rifle is widest across her back.
Second prop breadth axis at the skeleton buttstock near the image-left hip, where the rifle widens again.
Hair mass, image-left side: the bob sweeps well beyond the cranium, is widest near canvas y=100 and tucks back under the jaw.
Hair mass, image-right side: slightly narrower because the head turns that way, and it hangs lower, ending in tips below the jaw.
Face/jaw mass under the bangs, narrowing to the chin near canvas (243,140), still a plain plane with no features.
Short near-side neck mass bridging jaw to collar; most of the neck is occluded by hair and the raised collar.
Far side of the same neck bridge, meeting the collar mass.
Clothed torso mass, image-right contour from the observed jacket silhouette; widest near canvas y=340 at the near sleeve elbow.

Clothed torso mass, image-left contour, corrected on the reopened branch to the measured occupied volume: the loose jacket and the far hanging arm blouse out well past the shoulder line and reach their widest near canvas y=270-290.
Shallow cross-contour across the upper back, dropping toward the viewer to explain the back-three-quarter turn.
Second cross-contour at the belt band, explaining waist volume and the mild counter-twist.
Soft separation between the near sleeve mass and the torso mass, so the sleeve reads as its own tapered volume.
Inner boundary of the far sleeve mass, moved out with the corrected flank so the sleeve occupies the volume actually observed.
Pelvis basin, image-left: the shorts mass turns under the hip and flows into the thigh root instead of closing an ellipse.
Pelvis basin, image-right, narrowing faster and flowing into the braced thigh root.
Shorts hem across the support thigh, the first major internal break of the lower mass.
Shorts hem across the braced thigh, lower in frame because that leg is nearer the camera.
Support-leg mass, outer contour: bare thigh, a smooth swell through the sock top, a calf peak near canvas y=482 and a slim ankle.
Support-leg mass, inner contour; the thigh-to-ankle taper is asymmetric, not a parallel rail.
Braced-leg mass, outer contour: the wider, nearer leg, leaning image-right for its whole length.
Braced-leg mass, inner contour; the negative space between the legs is a tall wedge, wide at the knee and closing toward the hem.
Thigh pouch hanging on the braced leg: it owns the image-right silhouette between canvas y=405 and y=470, so it is stated as its own small mass rather than absorbed into the thigh.

Rifle mass, image-left contour, corrected on the reopened branch to the measured prop edge: a fat suppressor, an abrupt step to a near-vertical tapered handguard, then a widening receiver and stock. The earlier version leaned too far right through the middle.
Rifle mass, image-right contour: it steps out at the scope near canvas y=150 and again at the skeleton stock, so the long mass is not a plain rail.
Cross-contour across the widest part of the rifle mass, tying its two contours into one integrated volume.
Second cross-contour across the buttstock mass where it overlaps the image-left hip.
Near shoulder insertion: a short curved plane from the collar over the deltoid into the sleeve, so the arm emerges from the torso.
Far shoulder insertion, ending where the corrected flank takes the sleeve outward.
Near elbow as a short partial plane on the outer half of the sleeve, where the direction change is actually visible.
Short closing plane below the near elbow on the forearm side.
Far elbow transition, minimal because sleeve and rifle occlude it; placed on the corrected flank.
Near wrist: a short narrowing plane where the sleeve cuff meets the hand.
Near hand as a smooth wrist-to-palm volume with no finger detail; its lower-inner edge is left open where the pocket takes over, so it reads as occluded.
Occlusion mark where the near hand enters the pocket opening.
Far hand: only the partial block visible past the jacket hem and the rifle stock is stated.
Support-side pelvis-to-thigh insertion, a short plane offset from the hem rather than a second band.
Braced-side insertion, lower in frame because that hip is nearer the camera.
Support knee as a short partial directional plane across the front half of the leg.
Braced knee plane, tilted with that leg's outward lean.
Support ankle: a short narrowing bridge handing the leg mass to the boot.
Support boot as one simple grounded block: a shaft continuing the ankle direction, a toe swinging image-right and away, and a flat sole on the ground plane.
Sole/landing line of the far boot, verified against the subject's contact height.
Braced ankle bridge, lower and further image-right.
Braced boot as the larger near block; its toe swings further image-right and its sole lands lower because it is closest to the camera.
Sole/landing line of the near boot; the two sole heights preserve the support-versus-brace reading.
Sling strap leaving the near shoulder: the attachment that makes the rifle hang from her body.
Same strap continuing to the rifle; the gap between segments is the observed buckle, stated as a break, not drawn as a part.
Overlap mark where the rifle body passes in front of the torso; below the ownership handoff the garment is outside the prop, so this mark is now an internal boundary.
Attachment/overlap where the skeleton buttstock crosses the image-left hip.
Attachment plane of the thigh pouch: the strap that fixes it to the braced leg, so the pouch hangs rather than floats.
Decisive outer contour of the hair on the image-right, stated as one hair grouping without individual strands.
Decisive outer contour of the hair on the image-left, wider than the right because the head turns away from that side.
Decisive image-right silhouette of the jacket from the shoulder to the hem; the hair tips hand silhouette ownership to the garment here rather than riding down it.

Braced-leg outer silhouette from the pouch handoff down to the boot.
Near boot silhouette: shaft, toe swinging image-right, and the sole landing that is the lowest contact point in the picture.
Support-leg outer silhouette: the slimmer, more vertical of the two legs.
Far boot silhouette, smaller in frame and landing higher than the near boot.
Inner silhouette of the support leg, which together with its neighbour states the tall negative-space wedge between the legs.
Inner silhouette of the braced leg, closing the negative space against the support leg.
